title: Freezing a strain of C. elegans for long-term storage
author: Cristian Riccio
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.532g8qe
materials: The protocol is worded differently below:

steps.title: Prepare worm culture for freezing
steps.instruction: Pick 20 young adult C. elegans onto each of two (or three) 10 cm NGM plates seeded with 1 mL OP50 (total 40–60 worms). Grow at 15 °C for ~1 week or at 20 °C for ~4 days until plates contain little or no food, many L1/L2 larvae, some eggs, the correct phenotype, and no contamination.

steps.title: Harvest worms with M9
steps.instruction: Add ~5 mL M9 to each plate, swirl to loosen worms, then tilt the plate on its lid so the liquid drains to one side. Using a glass pipette, collect the worm‑containing liquid from each plate into a 15 mL conical tube (≈10 mL total).

steps.title: Pellet and wash worms
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at full speed for ~1 minute in a clinical centrifuge. Aspirate as much supernatant as possible without disturbing the pellet. Add ~15 mL fresh M9, resuspend the pellet, and spin again for ~1 minute at full speed. Repeat the wash if desired. Finally, aspirate all but ~3 mL of supernatant (or ~4.5 mL when using three plates).

steps.title: Add freezing solution
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of 2× freezing buffer (freezing solution) to the remaining worm suspension (e.g., 3 mL worm suspension + 3 mL 2× freezing buffer). Briefly agitate the tube to resuspend the worms evenly.

steps.title: Aliquot into labeled cryovials
steps.instruction: Dispense 1 mL of the worm‑freezing mixture into each of five sterile cryovials (or 6 vials for two plates, 9 vials for three plates). Label each vial with strain name, initials, date, and use BMP21 Plus Series Self‑laminating Polyester Cryogenic Laboratory Labels (Brady Worldwide, Catalog #M21-500-461) printed with a BMP21‑PLUS Portable Label Printer (Catalog #BMP21-PLUS).

steps.title: Freeze slowly in insulated container
steps.instruction: Place the cryovials into the styrofoam container that the 15 mL conical tubes come in, cover with a second styrofoam lid, secure with tape or rubber bands, and label the outside. Then put the container into a polystyrene box (which cools at ~1 °C per minute) and transfer the box to a –80 °C freezer (or –70 °C freezer space).

steps.title: Store cryovials after initial freeze
steps.instruction: After the first night, keep three cryovials in the –80 °C freezer and store one cryovial in liquid nitrogen as the master stock. When the –80 °C stock is exhausted, repeat the freezing procedure with a fresh culture.

steps.title: Thaw for viability check
steps.instruction: The next day, place a cryovial in a foam floater, submerge the floater in a glass of warm water until thawed, then pour the entire contents onto an NGM plate seeded with bacterial food. Incubate and, the following day, verify that at least 60 living worms are present.

steps.title: Assess survival and restock
steps.instruction: If the viability check is successful, retain three tubes in the –80 °C freezer and the master tube in liquid nitrogen; otherwise, repeat the freezing process with a new culture.

steps.title: Thaw for experimental use
steps.instruction: When a strain is needed, thaw a cryovial in warm water as above, allow worms to settle to the bottom, then use a pipette to draw up only the worm pellet with minimal liquid (do not pour the entire thawed suspension). Distribute the worms onto a fresh OP50‑seeded 6‑ or 10‑cm plate. Do not centrifuge, because glycerol in the freezing solution prevents pellet formation.

steps.title: Test thaw after one month
steps.instruction: Approximately one month after freezing, perform a test thaw as described. A successful freeze yields >10 surviving worms; pick several survivors onto a fresh plate and confirm they produce progeny of the correct phenotype before maintaining the line.
